#libraries
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(tigris)
library(sf)
library(stringr)
library(magick)
```

#load'n'look
```{r}
US_cases <- read.csv("US_case_incidence.csv")
US_cases <- US_cases %>%
  rename("2008" = "X2008", 
         "2009" = "X2009", 
         "2010" = "X2010", 
         "2011" = "X2011", 
         "2012" = "X2012", 
         "2012" = "X2012", 
         "2013" = "X2013", 
         "2014" = "X2014", 
         "2015" = "X2015", 
         "2016" = "X2016", 
         "2017" = "X2017", 
         "2018" = "X2018",
         "2019" = "X2019", 
         "2020" = "X2020", 
         "2021" = "X2021", 
         "2022" = "X2022", 
         "2023" = "X2023")

US_cases_longer <- pivot_longer(
    data = US_cases,
    cols = c("2008", "2009", "2010", "2011", "2012", "2013", "2014", "2015", "2016", "2017", "2018", "2019", "2020", "2021", "2022", "2023"),
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "Cases"
  )
US_cases_longer
max(US_cases_longer$Cases)
```

#heatmapping function
```{r}
dir_out <- file.path(".", "US_heatmaps_folder")
dir.create(dir_out, recursive = TRUE)

US_map <- states(cb = TRUE, year = 2024)
US_map <- US_map %>%
    rename("State" = "NAME")

US_cases_longer <- US_cases_longer %>%
  mutate(
    Year = as.numeric(Year),
    Cases = as.numeric(Cases)
  )

US_year_heatmap <- function(year_choice) {

#year by year, so filter the data by the year the user wants to see
  US_cases_year <- US_cases_longer %>%
    filter(Year == year_choice)

#join
merged_data <- left_join(US_map, US_cases_year, by = "State")

#standardizing across the entire range of case counts
case_limits <- c(0, 30000) #max cases per year in one state is ~22000, I think

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#remove case limits from above and below if we want to see states compare to
#each other in a certain year

#keep case limits if we're looking across the whole period of time
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#time to plot
heatmap <- ggplot(merged_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = Cases), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = case_limits, option = "plasma", name = "Number of Cases") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = paste("US Cases per State Heatmap in ", year_choice))
print(heatmap)

fp <- file.path(dir_out, paste0("US_case_heatmap_", year_choice, ".png"))

#time to save
ggsave(plot = heatmap, filename = fp, device = "png")

}

US_year_heatmap(2020)
```
